$comment: How the view looks from inside a fluid (docs/WATER_RENDERING.md §10, the waterline; owner, 2026-11-07: 'a clean waterline like this: currently our fog shows up too early and we don't have a clean line', with a photo of a camera half under clear tropical water). Per fluid, by its name in the block registry (a fluid not listed takes `default`). Each pixel is under the fluid when its view ray's point on the lens plane (lensM metres ahead of the eye along the camera's forward axis) is below the fluid's surface over the eye's column, raised and lowered by the line's waves: the screen splits along a straight, crisp line that moves smoothly with the eye's height (the drawn surface is flat, so the line's waves are the lens's, not the mesh's). lensM: how far ahead the lens plane is (m; larger, the line sweeps the screen more slowly as the eye rises or sinks: a level view's line reaches the screen's edge with the eye lensM × tan(half the vertical FOV) from the surface, 0.3 m for 0.4 at the default FOV). line.amplitudeM, line.wavelengthM, line.speed: the line's waves (m, m, cycles a second; amplitude 0: a straight line). meniscus: the thin bright band along the line where the surface meets the lens: color (sRGB), strength (0 to 1; 0: none) and widthPx (its half-width on screen, px of the drawing buffer). fog: the fluid's absorption and scattering (the block registry's fluid look) over the distance in the fluid, but only past clearM metres (0: from the eye) and scaled by density (1: the registry's own rates, as from above; lower reads clearer and farther, higher murkier). Run `node shared/look/underwater.mjs` after editing; CI fails if crates/dwell-look/src/underwater.gen.rs is stale. The content is prototype (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1).
